## Summary

**Root cause** (issue #333): CRLF/CR line-ending tolerance had been reinvented five separate times, each as its own narrow bug fix — `groundingMerge.ts`'s `\r?\n` in a diff3-marker regex, `hooks.ts`'s four `.replace(/\r/g, "")` calls, `gitignore.ts`'s `.replace(/\r$/, "")`, `docanchors.ts`'s `.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n")`, and `k8sManifest.ts`'s `\r?` sprinkled through its line regexes (plus its document-separator regex). No shared helper existed, so each new line-oriented scanner was guaranteed to reopen the same class of bug.

**Fix**: added `src/core/eol.ts` exporting `normalizeEol`, `lineContent`, and `sourceLines` (the last yields `{content, start}` per logical line, tolerant of LF/CRLF/lone-CR, with `start` always indexed against the *original* un-normalized string — needed because `k8sManifest.ts` reports character offsets into caller-supplied source). Rewired all five call sites onto it:

- `groundingMerge.ts` — matches its diff3 regex against a normalized copy, then restores CRLF in the result if the input was CRLF.
- `hooks.ts` / `gitignore.ts` — swapped their ad hoc `.replace(/\r.../ )` for `normalizeEol`/`lineContent`.
- `docanchors.ts` — swapped its `.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n")` for `normalizeEol`.
- `k8sManifest.ts` — switched its per-line scan and document-boundary detection to `sourceLines`, which also fixed a latent gap: lone-CR (Mac-style) line endings weren't previously split at all, since the old code only split on `\n`.

**Verified**: `npm run typecheck` is clean. `test/eol.test.ts` (2/2), `test/k8sManifest.test.ts` (97/97), and `test/grounding-merge-driver.test.ts` (11/13) pass — the 2 remaining failures spawn the real CLI via `tsx` as a subprocess and hit a sandbox-only `EPERM` on IPC-pipe creation; I confirmed via `git stash` that these same 2 tests fail identically with my changes fully reverted, so they're a pre-existing environment limitation, not a regression. I also ran the broader hooks/grounding/docanchors test files (204 tests) and confirmed the 13 failures there are byte-for-byte the same set with or without my change — same sandbox artifact, zero regressions introduced.
